raw_response:
*Speaking as the farmer, in her own voice:*

Aiya, what's to decide? Same as every year. Me and my old man been doing wheat then corn on this land forty years. Ten mu and a little bit — not big, not small, just enough for two old people to manage if we hire the tractor.

For the wheat, I plant around Cold Dew time, maybe October 8th or so — when my neighbor Old Wang starts, I start. I buy seed from the shop in town, the kind everyone buys, can't remember the name but the shopkeeper knows. Before plowing I spread one bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind, that's what the shop has. Then in spring when the wheat turns green, I scatter half a bag of urea per mu. If it looks yellow I put a little more, if it looks good I save some. I water before the ground freezes in winter, and once in spring when it's jointing. If no rain comes before harvest I water one more time, but water costs money from the well so I don't like to.

For the corn right after wheat harvest in June — no time to rest, the ground has to go back in right away or you lose days. I buy hybrid corn seed, everyone does now, the old kinds don't yield. Hire the direct-seeder to put it in, maybe 3-4 kg seed per mu. One bag compound fertilizer at planting, then when it reaches the big flare stage I scatter urea again. Summer usually has rain so maybe one irrigation, maybe none.

My husband and I can't do heavy work anymore, so we pay for plowing, sowing, spraying, harvesting. Herbicide I spray once each crop, that's standard. Bug spray only if I see bugs. Last year wheat gave me about 400 kg per mu, corn maybe 450 — that's normal. If I get the same this year, I'm satisfied.
